--- title: "Verbal short-term memory (15 CVC syllables)" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · HFON_MEMVERB_MEMORIA_VERBAL_CVC_1_5" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (F · Span and memory; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea HFON_MEMVERB_MEMORIA_VERBAL_CVC_1_5`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Memoria verbal (1–5 sílabas CVC)*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/HFON_MEMVERB_MEMORIA_VERBAL_CVC_1_5.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Verbal short-term memory (1–5 CVC syllables), at age 7 (818 administrations in 1 cohorts). AUC .50 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 2261 | | Battery | DIS-ESP | | Format | auditory stimuli | | Items | — | | Task family | F · Span and memory | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | INSTRUCCIONES: El alumno/a no puede ver la pantalla del ordenador Con auriculares La prueba consta de 15 ítems. Los tres primeros ítems son una sola sílaba cada uno, los tres siguientes son series de dos sílabas, los tres que siguen tienen tres sílabas, las siguientes cuatro sílabas y los tres últimos constan de cinco silabas cada uno. *(Spanish)* | ## Theoretical framework Repeating sequences of nonsense syllables, from one to five syllables, measures **phonological short-term memory**: keeping in order a series of sounds that are not supported by meaning. It is related to reading because decoding requires holding the sounds of the letters while they are blended. The versions use CV or CVC syllables. **What the evidence says:** - **It adds little beyond phonemic awareness.** A meta-analysis concludes that phonemic awareness is the strongest unique predictor of reading. Longitudinal and experimental studies support its causal role, but not that of verbal short-term memory [@melbylervag2012stm]. In a study from preschool to Grade 3, verbal memory did not predict reading once phonological awareness and RAN were controlled [@parrila2004predictors]. - **Serial order does seem to count at the start.** In 780 children followed from age 4 to 9, serial order memory predicted word reading from age 4 to 6, and reading did not influence it. Pseudoword repetition and reading influenced each other in both directions [@cunningham2021memory]. - **In dyslexia the deficit exists, but it depends on oral language.** Children with dyslexia repeat pseudowords worse than children of their age and than younger readers at the same reading level. Severity varies widely across studies and is explained mainly by oral language level, that is, by co-occurrence with developmental language disorder [@melbylervag2012nonword]. We have not found longitudinal studies in Spanish with this task. **What our data show.** - **Main version (15 items, ages 4 to 7).** α (2021) = .76 and stability across school years ρ = .36 (range .23–.44, about 12 months apart). Its validity grows with age: AUC against persistent difficulty of .58 at age 4, .61 at age 5 and .66–.72 at ages 6–7. Against later low comprehension, .58–.65. The ceiling effect is moderate (4–12%). - **Full version at age 8.** AUC of .63 against persistent difficulty and of .62–.66 against Woodcock-Muñoz. - **CVC version of 1–5 syllables (age 7).** The observed maximum is 3, 86% of children are at ceiling and the AUC is .50. This looks like a recording or scoring error, not a result about the construct: it should not be used until it has been reviewed. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 7.2| 2010| 189|2017/18 | 818| 255| 562| 31| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 7.2| 255| 2010| 2.84| 0.41| 3| -2.68| 0| 86.27| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|-------:| | 7.2| 255|1–3 |1–3 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Word and text reading (7.2, r = .06). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .50. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .50. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_HFON_MEMVERB_MEMORIA_VERBAL_CVC_1_5_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .52 (1 time point; 256–256 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 7.2| 255| 2010| 2| 2| 3| 3| 3| 3| 3| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_HFON_MEMVERB_MEMORIA_VERBAL_CVC_1_5_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 7.2| 749| 0.072| 0.049| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.2| 814| 0.032| 0.651| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.2| 813| 0.050| 0.154| |School (ICC) | 7.2| 818| 0.107| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Verbal short-term memory (1–5 CVC syllables)” (code 2261; DIS-ESP battery) assesses phonological short-term memory. Stimuli are presented auditorily and the child responds by selecting on the screen. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010 cohorts it was administered in 1 session, from 7 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .50. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 7.2 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
